I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation on our 3 mu for forty years now, so I know this land well. With high school education I read the bags and keep track of costs, but I also watch what my neighbors do and what works on our plot. Our ground here in Quzhou is decent loam, but after so many years of double cropping the soil is tired, so I keep fertilizer steady — can't cut back or yield drops. My husband and I mostly do the work ourselves; two of our children send money from the city, so we're not desperate, but 3 mu is small and every yuan counts.

For winter wheat in October, I'll plant Jimai 22 or a similar improved variety — about 15 kg seed per mu since I drill a bit thick to cover any poor germination. Base fertilizer I mix myself: one bag (40 kg) of compound 15-15-15 per mu before rotary tillage, that gives me 6 kg each of N, P, K upfront. Then at jointing in March I topdress 15 kg urea per mu — roughly 7 kg more N. Total about 13 kg N, 6 kg P2O5, 6 kg K2O — a bit less than neighbors who pile on 20+ kg N, but I've learned more doesn't help once the soil is saturated. Irrigation: winter water in November, then jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling if dry — usually 3 times, sometimes 4. Spray herbicide once in spring, then one mix for aphids and powdery mildew at heading, maybe a second if rust shows. I expect 500 kg/mu, good years 550.

For summer maize right after wheat harvest in June, I no-till plant Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid — 2 kg seed per mu, direct seed into wheat stubble. Apply one bag of compound 15-15-15 at sowing and 15 kg urea at big trumpet stage — total around 14 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K. The well runs if July-August is dry, usually 1-2 irrigations. Spray once for borer when silks show, sometimes a second for armyworm. I expect 550 kg/mu.
